{'new_text': 'Apple has updated its official list of digital camera RAW formats supported on its platforms, adding support for 11 new models from multiple manufacturers. Details below.', 'type': 'translation'}

{'new_text': 'Apple now supports RAW files from 562 cameras', 'type': 'translation'}

{'new_text': "Apple's operating systems provide system-level support for processing RAW images captured by a wide range of third-party cameras.", 'type': 'translation'}

{'new_text': 'In simple terms, this allows compatible apps to handle RAW files from those cameras directly, giving users more flexibility to adjust exposure, colour and other elements.', 'type': 'translation'}

{'new_text': 'Compared with formats such as JPEG, the latter simply cannot offer the same flexibility in post-production editing, because most of the image processing is essentially "baked in" and written directly into the final image.', 'type': 'translation'}

{'new_text': 'Apple has long maintained a support article listing the digital camera RAW formats supported by its current (and past) operating systems. That list was updated today, adding 11 new digital cameras and bringing the total to 562 models.', 'type': 'translation'}
